title: The Statue in New York Harbor
description: Explore the Statue of Liberty through familiar shapes, symbolic objects, and the material of its outer skin.
cardDescription: Explore the Statue of Liberty through familiar shapes, symbolic objects, and the material of its outer skin.
subtheme: The Statue in New York Harbor
focus: The statue’s symbolic objects, metal surface, and harbor setting offer several ways to recognize the landmark. An object held by the figure has a different name from the whole figure.
solvingTip: Separate the figure from the objects it holds. Use an object or a harbor feature to begin, then try the material and country names.
words: Freedom represented by New York Harbor's famous robed statue
Raised light-bearing object held by the Statue of Liberty
Metal forming the Statue of Liberty's outer skin
Raised supporting base beneath a statue
Country that gave the Statue of Liberty to the United States
Sculpted figure standing on a supporting base
Headpiece worn by the Statue of Liberty
Inscribed object held against the statue's body
Long garment represented on the statue
Water-surrounded land supporting the statue's site
Sheltered water associated with the statue's New York setting
State associated with the famous Liberty statue, with spaces omitted
Stairway units leading upward in a large structure
Light or symbol serving as a guide

answerNotes.LIBERTY: Liberty is the idea represented by the statue. It names the concept rather than the pedestal beneath the figure.
answerNotes.TORCH: The torch is held aloft. The tablet is a different object held closer to the figure's body.
answerNotes.COPPER: The outer copper surface developed its green patina over time. The statue was not originally painted green to create that appearance.
answerNotes.PEDESTAL: A pedestal supports the figure. It is separate from the figure's robe, crown, and symbolic objects.
answerNotes.FRANCE: The statue was a gift from France. The American pedestal and the French-made statue formed separate parts of the project.

title: Across the Golden Gate
description: Explore a famous suspension bridge through cables, towers, water, and its recognizable color.
cardDescription: Explore a famous suspension bridge through cables, towers, water, and its recognizable color.
focus: The bridge spans the Golden Gate strait. Its name refers to that water passage, while structural clues identify the parts carrying and supporting a roadway.
solvingTip: Look for a bridge part, a land or water feature, or a color word. The names and structures provide different entry points.
words: San Francisco strait spanned by a famous suspension bridge, with spaces omitted
Long tension member helping support a suspension bridge
Color completing the bridge's official shade, International ___
California county at the north end of the Golden Gate Bridge
Narrow water passage beneath the Golden Gate Bridge
Structure carrying a roadway across a gap or waterway
Tall bridge support rising above the roadway
Strong metal alloy used in suspension-bridge construction
Low cloud often associated with the San Francisco coast
Sheltered water body east of the Golden Gate strait
Ocean west of the Golden Gate
To secure a bridge cable firmly at its end

answerNotes.GOLDENGATE: Golden Gate is the name of the strait as well as the bridge. The bridge's color is a separate clue.
answerNotes.CABLE: Suspension cables carry loads through tension. A roadway deck is a different part of the structure.
answerNotes.ORANGE: International Orange is the familiar bridge color name. It is distinct from the gold suggested by Golden Gate.
answerNotes.MARIN: The bridge links San Francisco with Marin County. The clue asks for the county name rather than the strait.
answerNotes.STRAIT: A strait connects larger bodies of water. Golden Gate is the passage between San Francisco Bay and the Pacific.

title: A View into the Grand Canyon
description: Explore a great Arizona landscape through its river, rock layers, rims, and deep-cut landforms.
cardDescription: Explore a great Arizona landscape through its river, rock layers, rims, and deep-cut landforms.
subtheme: A View into the Grand Canyon
focus: The named river and state anchor the scene. Other clues describe landform shapes and long-term erosion rather than giving a hiking itinerary.
solvingTip: Use a familiar river or state name first. A clue about an upper edge differs from one about the deep land below it.
words: River flowing through the Grand Canyon
US state containing Grand Canyon National Park
Wearing away and carrying off soil by wind or water
Upper edge of a large canyon
One distinct bed visible in a stack of rock
Deep steep-sided valley carved through rock
Natural flowing watercourse at the bottom of a canyon
Solid natural material exposed in canyon walls
Deep narrow valley with steep rock sides
Steep exposed rock face along high ground
Broad raised land with a relatively level top
US distance unit used for a park road or trail
Wide scenic view from an overlook
Path followed on foot through a landscape

answerNotes.COLORADO: The Colorado River flows through the canyon. It should not be confused with the state of Colorado, which shares its name.
answerNotes.ARIZONA: Grand Canyon National Park is in Arizona. The clue asks for the state rather than the river.
answerNotes.EROSION: Erosion removes and transports material. It helps explain a landscape over time rather than one brief event.
answerNotes.RIM: A rim is an upper edge. It differs from the river channel far below.
answerNotes.LAYER: A rock layer is one bed within a larger sequence. Different layers can record different conditions in the past.

title: Four Faces at Mount Rushmore
description: Explore the carved monument through its stone, setting, sculptor, and presidential figures.
cardDescription: Explore the carved monument through its stone, setting, sculptor, and presidential figures.
focus: The clues name the Mount Rushmore sculpture and selected features of it. The Black Hills also have a wider history and significance beyond the monument.
solvingTip: Separate a figure’s surname from a material or a land feature. Short shape and counting words help cross longer names.
words: Mountain with four large carved presidential faces
Hard rock into which the Rushmore faces were carved
Number of presidential faces on Mount Rushmore
President represented alongside Jefferson, Roosevelt, and Lincoln
Surname of Gutzon, the sculptor associated with Mount Rushmore
Artwork shaped or carved in three dimensions
Fronts of heads represented in the monument
Thomas among the presidents carved at Mount Rushmore
Theodore among the presidents carved at Mount Rushmore
Abraham among the presidents carved at Mount Rushmore
Raised landforms in the region named the Black ___
General word for the material a carver shapes
Edged tool associated with shaping stone
To shape a figure by removing material
Scene seen when looking toward a monument

answerNotes.RUSHMORE: Mount Rushmore is in the Black Hills of South Dakota. The area is sacred to the Lakota and has a history beyond the sculpture.
answerNotes.GRANITE: Granite is the rock material. The clue does not ask for a president or the sculptor.
answerNotes.FOUR: The monument shows four presidents. Counting the figures is different from identifying their individual surnames.
answerNotes.WASHINGTON: George Washington is one of the four figures. The clue uses the surname rather than the capital city named after him.
answerNotes.BORGLUM: Gutzon Borglum led the monument's design and carving. His son Lincoln Borglum also worked on the project.

title: The Tall Monument on the Mall
description: Explore the Washington Monument through its tapered form, stone materials, and pointed top.
cardDescription: Explore the Washington Monument through its tapered form, stone materials, and pointed top.
subtheme: The Tall Monument on the Mall
focus: The monument is an obelisk built from blocks, rather than one enormous single stone. Clues combine its setting with clear shape and construction words.
solvingTip: Look for a form, a material, or a place around the structure. A support at the bottom and a point at the top have different names.
words: Tall four-sided tapering monument with a pyramid-shaped top
Stone forming much of the Washington Monument's exterior
Metal forming the Washington Monument's small pyramidal tip
National ___: Washington park setting of the monument
Lowest supporting portion of a tall monument
US president honored by the tall monument on the National Mall
Hard stone also used in the monument's construction
Natural building material cut into monument blocks
Sharp tip at the top of a tapered structure
City serving as the seat of a nation's government
Vertical distance from a monument's bottom to its top
Open public area near a large structure
Visible expanse behind the top of a tall monument

answerNotes.OBELISK: An obelisk has a tapering shaft and pointed top. The Washington Monument uses this form but is built from many blocks.
answerNotes.MARBLE: Marble forms much of the exterior. The structure also incorporates other materials rather than being one solid marble block.
answerNotes.ALUMINUM: The cap is aluminum, using the common American spelling. It is a small part of the monument rather than the main exterior stone.
answerNotes.MALL: The National Mall is a public landscape in Washington, DC. Mall does not mean a shopping center in this clue.
answerNotes.BASE: The base is the bottom portion. Its position contrasts with the pointed top rather than naming a material.
